club: Maples Tech Club (MTC) — Learn it. Build it. Ship it.

questions.question_text: Which shortcut CUTS (moves) selected text so you can paste it somewhere else?
While watching a video on YouTube or VLC, pressing the Spacebar usually does what?
Which shortcut opens the PRINT box to print a page or save it as a PDF?
In Word or Google Docs, what does pressing Ctrl + B do to selected text?
In a document editor, which shortcut makes selected text Italic (slanted)?
In a document editor, which shortcut UNDERLINES the selected words?
What is the difference between the Backspace key and the Delete key while typing?
questions.option_b: Backspace erases to the left of the cursor; Delete erases to the right of the cursor
questions.option_c: Both do the exact same thing

questions.question_text: If you want to quickly FIND a specific word on a long webpage or PDF, which shortcut do you press?
Which key at the top-left of the keyboard is commonly pressed to cancel a pop-up or exit full-screen video?
Which function key is the classic shortcut to REFRESH or reload a webpage in a browser?
If you pressed Ctrl + Z (Undo) by mistake and want your change back, which shortcut performs REDO?
Which keyboard shortcut lets you quickly switch between open apps/windows on Windows?
To type a single capital letter or the "@" symbol above the number 2 without turning on Caps Lock, which key do you hold?
Which shortcut opens a brand-new blank document or window in most apps?
In a web browser like Chrome or Edge, what does pressing Ctrl + T do?
In a web browser, what does pressing Ctrl + W do?
Which key on a Windows keyboard is used to capture a screenshot of your entire screen?
When a file or folder is selected on Windows, pressing which function key lets you RENAME it immediately?
Which pocket-sized device plugs into a USB port to carry files between home and school?
On a laptop, what is the flat touch-sensitive rectangle below the keyboard that works like a mouse?
Pressing the RIGHT button on a computer mouse usually opens what?
questions.option_d: A small shortcut/context menu with helpful options

questions.question_text: Which classroom device shines your computer screen onto a large white wall or board so the whole class can watch?
On a smartphone or tablet, the screen both shows pictures AND senses your finger taps. What is it called?
What Does "Hardware" mean in simple everyday words?
questions.option_b: The physical parts of a computer that you can actually see and touch

questions.question_text: In Indian homes and school labs, a small box called a UPS is connected to desktop PCs. Why is it useful?
questions.option_d: It provides short battery backup during a power cut so you can save your work safely

questions.question_text: What is the opposite of a Printer — a device that turns a paper certificate or drawing into a digital image file on your PC?
Which single modern cable carries BOTH sharp high-definition video AND audio from a laptop to a TV or projector?
At a supermarket checkout or school library, which handheld device reads black-and-white striped labels instantly?
Why can a laptop keep running during a power cut even without an external UPS?
questions.option_c: Laptops have a built-in rechargeable battery inside

questions.question_text: What is the tiny removable storage card used inside many cameras and Android phones called?
What is the main job of the small spinning fan inside a laptop or desktop cabinet?
questions.option_b: To blow dust onto the screen
questions.option_c: To keep the processor and internal parts cool so the computer does not overheat

questions.question_text: In everyday phones and computers, what is the simple difference between RAM and Storage (SSD/ROM)?
questions.option_b: RAM stores photos forever; Storage deletes everything on restart
questions.option_c: RAM holds active apps temporarily while working; Storage keeps your photos and files saved even when powered off
questions.option_d: Both are names for the screen

questions.question_text: If your computer opens 15 browser tabs and starts feeling sluggish when switching apps, having more of which part helps most?
Modern laptops use an SSD instead of an older spinning Hard Disk (HDD). What everyday benefit do you notice right away?
questions.option_a: The laptop boots up and opens apps much faster, with no moving disk parts
questions.option_c: You never need to charge the battery

questions.question_text: Which newer oval-shaped reversible charging/data port is found on almost all modern Android phones and newer laptops?
What do we call the main circuit board inside a computer that connects the processor, RAM, storage, and ports together?
Look at the file name "annual_day_photo.jpg". What kind of file is it?
Look at the file name "school_anthem.mp3". What kind of file is it?
Look at the file name "science_fair_demo.mp4". What kind of file is it?
What are the three small buttons ( — , □ , ✕ ) at the top-right corner of almost every Windows app window for?
questions.option_b: Minimize, Maximize, and Close the window

questions.question_text: Which popular design app/website lets students easily create posters, certificates, and invitations using ready templates?
What does "Software" mean in simple everyday language?
questions.option_a: Soft cloth used to clean a monitor
questions.option_c: The power socket on the wall
questions.option_d: The apps, programs, and operating system that run inside a computer or phone

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an Operating System (the core system software that runs a PC or phone)?
Why do schools send circulars and admit cards as a ".pdf" file instead of an editable Word file?
questions.option_b: PDFs keep the exact layout, fonts, and alignment looking identical on every phone and computer
questions.option_c: PDFs do not take even 1 byte of space

questions.question_text: Which application is best suited for keeping an attendance list, marks table, or club budget with automatic totals?
What is the difference between "Copy & Paste" and "Cut & Paste" on a file?
questions.option_d: Copy leaves the original file in place and makes a duplicate; Cut moves the file to the new folder

questions.question_text: What is a ".zip" file commonly used for when sharing a project?
questions.option_d: Bundling many files/folders together into one smaller compressed file for easy sending

questions.question_text: In Word or Google Docs, what is the difference between "Save" and "Save As"?
questions.option_b: "Save" updates the current file; "Save As" lets you save a separate copy with a new name or location
questions.option_d: Both print the document on paper

questions.question_text: Which long bar at the bottom of a Windows screen shows the Start button, pinned apps, and clock?
Why do many students turn on "Dark Mode" in apps when reading or working in the evening?
questions.option_a: It uses a dark background that feels gentler on the eyes in low light
questions.option_c: It prints pages in black paper
questions.option_d: It makes Wi-Fi twice as fast

questions.question_text: If you want to jot down a quick plain-text note with zero heavy formatting, which lightweight built-in Windows app opens instantly?
When saving an image with a transparent background (such as a school logo), which image format supports transparency cleanly?
On Windows, files ending in ".exe" (or ".apk" on Android) are what kind of files?
questions.option_c: Application installer / executable program files (only run from trusted official sources!)

questions.question_text: Before editing an important project presentation, why is naming files clearly like "Science_Poster_v2_Final.pptx" better than "asdf123.pptx"?
questions.option_c: Computers refuse to save short names
questions.option_d: Clear file names let you and your teammates find the right version in seconds without confusion

questions.question_text: What is the website address typed at the top of a browser (like `https://mapleskhatauli.com`) commonly called?
What does the Left Arrow (←) "Back" button at the top-left of a browser do?
questions.option_d: Takes you back to the previous webpage you were just viewing

questions.question_text: Look at an email address: `student@mapleskhatauli.com`. Which symbol always separates the username from the domain name?
What is that square black-and-white patterned box on posters or ID cards that opens a link when scanned with a phone camera?
Which of these is ALSO a popular web browser besides Google Chrome?
questions.option_a: Mozilla Firefox / Microsoft Edge / Apple Safari

questions.question_text: If you visited a helpful website yesterday and forgot its name, which browser list helps you find it again?
What is the real difference between Google Chrome and Google Search?
questions.option_a: Chrome is a search website; Google is a laptop brand
questions.option_b: Chrome is the Browser app installed on your device; Google Search is a website used inside a browser to look up info

questions.question_text: When you see `https://` and a padlock icon in the browser address bar before logging in, what does the "s" in `https` mean?
questions.option_c: Secure — data between your browser and the website is encrypted so others on Wi-Fi cannot read your password

questions.question_text: What does opening an "Incognito" or "Private" browser window ACTUALLY do on a shared computer?
questions.option_a: It blocks all computer viruses automatically
questions.option_b: It gives free unlimited mobile data
questions.option_c: It makes you completely invisible to websites and your internet provider
questions.option_d: It stops the browser from saving your browsing history, cookies, and login session on THAT computer after you close the window

questions.question_text: If a webpage shows "404 — Page Not Found", what does that simply mean?
questions.option_d: The specific link or page was moved, deleted, or typed with a spelling mistake

questions.question_text: When writing a polite email to a teacher or competition organizer, why should you always fill in the "Subject" line?
questions.option_a: Subject is where you type your password
questions.option_b: So the receiver immediately knows what your email is about before even opening it
questions.option_c: Emails cannot be sent without 50 words in Subject

questions.question_text: If an expected registration confirmation email has not arrived in your Inbox, which email folder should you check next?
Why do websites sometimes ask you to tick "I am not a robot" or pick traffic lights (CAPTCHA)?
questions.option_a: To stop automated spam bots from creating fake accounts or flooding forms
questions.option_d: To test your eyesight for driving

questions.question_text: In Chrome or Edge, which shortcut opens your recent Downloads list directly inside the browser?
What are website "Cookies" in everyday browsing?
questions.option_b: Tiny text files saved by websites in your browser to remember things like your login status or dark-mode preference

questions.question_text: In Google Search, putting quotation marks around an exact phrase like `"Maples Academy Khatauli"` helps you find:
questions.option_a: Pages that do NOT mention Maples Academy
questions.option_c: Pages containing that exact phrase with those words together in that order

questions.question_text: What is Google Drive or Microsoft OneDrive an example of?
questions.option_c: A physical pendrive inside your pocket
questions.option_d: Cloud storage — lets you save files online and open or share them from any phone or computer

questions.question_text: When sharing a Google Drive project link with your teacher, why should you check whether access is set to "Restricted" vs "Anyone with the link can View"?
questions.option_b: View access lets anyone delete your account
questions.option_d: If left "Restricted", your teacher will see "Access Denied" when clicking your submitted link!

questions.question_text: When you select a photo FROM your computer and post/submit it TO an online portal, is that called Downloading or Uploading?
Look at the curved fan-shaped icon with 3 or 4 arcs in the corner of your phone or laptop screen. What does it show?
Which of these tasks works completely OFFLINE even when you have zero internet connection?
questions.option_c: Using the built-in Calculator or typing in Notepad

questions.question_text: Why do home and school Wi-Fi networks have a password?
questions.option_a: So strangers outside cannot use your internet or access devices on your network
questions.option_b: To make the router light turn blue
questions.option_d: Because routers cannot turn on without a 20-letter name

questions.question_text: When a YouTube video pauses with a spinning circle in the middle because the internet is slow, what is that called?
Roughly how far does normal Bluetooth (like wireless earbuds connected to your phone) usually reach clearly?
questions.option_b: A short room-size distance (around 10 meters / 30 feet)

questions.question_text: Your laptop says "Connected to Wi-Fi, No Internet." What does this message actually mean?
questions.option_c: Your laptop is connected to the Wi-Fi router in the room, but the router’s outside internet line is down
questions.option_d: Your laptop Wi-Fi card is broken

questions.question_text: Why are desktop computers in an exam lab often connected by Ethernet (LAN) cables instead of Wi-Fi?
questions.option_b: LAN cables also power the monitor without electricity
questions.option_c: Desktop PCs can never use Wi-Fi
questions.option_d: A wired Ethernet cable gives steadier, interference-free internet for 30+ PCs at the same time

questions.question_text: Internet plan speeds from providers like JioFiber, Airtel, or BSNL are commonly advertised in "100 Mbps". What does Mbps measure?
questions.option_a: How many months the plan lasts
questions.option_c: How far the Wi-Fi reaches in meters
questions.option_d: Megabits per second — how fast data transfers over your internet connection

questions.question_text: Companies like BSNL, Airtel, Jio, or local fiber broadband providers that connect homes/schools to the internet are called:
Why does Wi-Fi signal become weaker when you walk three rooms away behind thick concrete walls?
questions.option_c: Thick walls and distance absorb and weaken wireless radio waves from the router

questions.question_text: What is a "Local Area Network (LAN)" in simple everyday words?
questions.option_a: Computers, laptops, and printers connected together inside one building, home, or school campus

questions.question_text: If ONE Wi-Fi printer is connected to the school office Wi-Fi router, how many computers on that same Wi-Fi can print to it?
questions.option_a: All authorized computers/phones on that same Wi-Fi network can share and print to it wirelessly
questions.option_c: Only a computer plugged into it with an HDMI cable
questions.option_d: Only phones with no SIM card

questions.question_text: When you mirror your phone or laptop screen wirelessly onto a classroom Smart TV without any cable, what is that feature called?
Every device connected to a network gets an identifying number address (like a house number for delivering data packets). What is it called?
You are using a 1.5 GB/day mobile data pack via Hotspot. Watching 2 hours of video at `4K / 2160p` vs `480p` will do what?
questions.option_d: `4K` uses many times more mobile data and can finish your 1.5 GB pack very quickly!

questions.question_text: On a laptop connected to someone’s mobile Hotspot, turning ON "Metered Connection" (or Data Saver) helps because:
questions.option_d: It pauses huge background Windows updates so your friend’s mobile data does not drain suddenly

questions.question_text: On modern dual-band home Wi-Fi routers, you often see two Wi-Fi names: `Home_2.4G` and `Home_5G`. What is the practical difference?
questions.option_b: `5 GHz` gives faster speeds nearby in the same room; `2.4 GHz` reaches farther through walls
questions.option_c: `5G` Wi-Fi requires a 5G SIM card inside the router
questions.option_d: There is no difference at all

questions.question_text: Why shouldn’t you eat sticky snacks or keep an open cup of water right over a computer keyboard?
questions.option_b: Crumbs and spilled liquid can permanently short-circuit and ruin the keyboard or laptop

questions.question_text: If a pop-up flashes on screen: "🎉 CONGRATULATIONS! You won a free iPhone! Click here & enter your details!", what is it almost certainly?
questions.option_b: A real gift from your browser
questions.option_c: A scam / phishing trap trying to steal personal details or install malware — close it immediately!

questions.question_text: What is "Netiquette"?
questions.option_a: Good manners, kindness, and respectful behavior when communicating on the internet

questions.question_text: Should you share your home address, school timetable, and phone number publicly with unknown strangers in online game chats?
questions.option_a: No — keep personal details private to stay safe online
questions.option_b: Yes, if they offer free game coins
questions.option_c: Yes, if they have a cool profile picture
questions.option_d: Yes, on every public comment section

questions.question_text: When you use a diagram, photo, or quote created by someone else in your school presentation, what is the honest thing to do?
questions.option_a: Crop out their name and claim it as yours
questions.option_b: Give clear credit to the original creator or source instead of pretending you made it yourself
questions.option_d: Forbid anyone else from seeing the source

questions.question_text: To keep your eyes comfortable while studying or working on a computer, what does the healthy "20-20-20 Rule" recommend?
questions.option_c: Every 20 minutes, look at something 20 feet away for 20 seconds to relax your eyes
questions.option_d: Sit 20 millimeters from the screen for 20 hours

questions.question_text: Important UPI Safety Rule in India: Do you EVER need to enter your secret UPI PIN to RECEIVE money from someone?
questions.option_a: UPI PIN is just your roll number
questions.option_b: Yes, scanning any QR code automatically credits money after PIN
questions.option_c: Yes, you must enter UPI PIN to receive gifts
questions.option_d: NEVER! A UPI PIN is ONLY entered when money is GOING OUT from your account — asking you to enter PIN to "receive" money is a scam!

questions.question_text: What is "Two-Factor Authentication (2FA)" on email or social accounts, and why is it great?
questions.option_a: It forces two friends to share one account
questions.option_b: It slows down typing speed by half
questions.option_c: It deletes your account after two days
questions.option_d: It adds a second check (like a code on your phone) besides your password, so thieves can’t break in with a leaked password alone

questions.question_text: Why is reusing the EXACT SAME password across 10 different games, websites, and your main email risky?
questions.option_a: It uses extra storage on your phone
questions.option_b: If even one small game site gets hacked, attackers immediately try that same password on your email and other accounts!

questions.question_text: How should a responsible student use AI tools (like ChatGPT or Gemini) when working on a project or assignment?
questions.option_b: Copy-paste the entire AI output without reading a word and sign it as 100% your own
questions.option_c: Use AI to brainstorm, understand tough ideas, or debug — then write/build in your own understanding and honestly mention where AI helped
questions.option_d: Trust every single date or quote from AI without checking

questions.question_text: You install a simple "Flashlight" app on a phone, and it suddenly asks permission to read your Contacts, Call Logs, and Messages. What should you think?
questions.option_a: Deny/uninstall! A flashlight only needs the camera LED — asking for private contacts and messages is a big privacy red flag
questions.option_b: Flashlights need your contacts to shine brighter

questions.question_text: What is "Phishing"?
questions.option_a: Fake emails, SMS, or look-alike websites pretending to be a trusted bank/company to trick you into typing passwords or OTPs

questions.question_text: What does your "Digital Footprint" mean?
questions.option_a: Walking barefoot in the computer lab
questions.option_b: The lasting trail of posts, comments, photos, and public activity associated with you on the internet
questions.option_c: The size of your laptop in inches

questions.question_text: Why is downloading "Cracked / Pirated" paid software or game cheats from shady websites dangerous as well as unethical?
questions.option_b: Official free alternatives like VLC, GIMP, or LibreOffice do not exist
questions.option_c: Besides disrespecting creators’ work, pirated cracks are one of the #1 ways password-stealing malware infects home PCs!
questions.option_d: Cracked software runs faster and safer than official apps

questions.question_text: Before clicking "Save Password" when Chrome asks on a shared school or cyber-café computer, what should you ALWAYS choose?
questions.option_a: Share it with the café owner
questions.option_b: Write your password on a sticky note on the monitor
questions.option_c: Click "Save" so you never have to type again
questions.option_d: Click "Never" — saving your password on a shared computer lets the next person log straight into your account!

questions.question_text: In a class study WhatsApp/Telegram group, what keeps the group helpful and respectful for everyone?
questions.option_a: Sending 80 stickers in a row at midnight
questions.option_b: Starting personal arguments in front of 60 people
questions.option_d: Keeping messages relevant, polite, avoiding late-night spam chains, and respecting classmates’ opinions

questions.question_text: Why do phones and Windows regularly release "Security Updates"?
questions.option_b: To patch newly discovered security holes so hackers and malware cannot exploit them

questions.question_text: If a classmate accidentally left their Gmail open on a school lab computer, what is the ONLY ethical thing to do?
questions.option_b: Read their private emails for fun
questions.option_c: Immediately click "Sign Out" without reading a single email, and politely let them know to be careful next time
questions.option_d: Send a prank email from their account
